transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess things have been getting a little weird at work. What really scared everyone is that I started freezing up right in the middle of service, or just... doing things completely out of order. Like, the other day I was just standing over by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I was just repeating table numbers out loud over and over instead of actually closing out my checks. It really freaked my manager and my coworkers out, so they wanted me to come see someone.
Do you remember what happened during that episode, or did you only learn about it because your coworkers told you?

Honestly, I... I don't really remember it. It's kind of a blur. I only know the details because my manager pulled me into the office afterward and told me what I was doing. I guess I just... wasn't really there for a minute. So yeah, I mostly just know what they told me.
Right before one of these episodes happens, do you notice any unusual sensations or warning signs?

No, not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. It's just... I'll be working, you know, taking an order or walking to a table, and I feel completely normal. There's no warning or strange feeling right before it happens. It just kind of comes out of nowhere.
About how long do these episodes typically last?

I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. Since I don't really remember them happening, it's hard to say. My manager said the one by the soda station felt like it went on for a few minutes before someone finally snapped me out of it, but... I don't really know for sure.
Right after an episode finishes, how do you feel physically and mentally?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't think I feel any different. When I... you know, when someone gets my attention and I realize what happened, I just feel normal. 

Physically I feel fine. Mentally, I guess I'm just a little confused because suddenly people are looking at me or asking if I'm okay, but I don't feel sick or exhausted or anything like that. I just feel like myself, like no time even passed.

What really scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service, or I'd be doing things completely out of order. Like that time by the soda station... I was standing there holding the cash drawer key, and apparently I was just repeating table numbers over and over instead of actually closing out the checks. But yeah, if someone talks to me or gets my attention, I snap out of it.
Do you ever notice gaps in your memory or feel like you have lost time in your everyday life outside of work?

No, not really. I don't think I lose time when I'm just going about my normal day. Like, if I'm at home or out running errands, my memory is fine. I haven't noticed any missing hours or gaps like you're saying. It really just seems to be those specific moments at the restaurant that people have pointed out to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experiences transient dissociative episodes marked by unresponsiveness, behavioral arrest, automatic vocalizations (repeating table numbers), and localized amnesia without typical postictal fatigue or confusion. The ability to be abruptly terminated by external sensory stimulation and the clear temporal relationship with prolonged workplace stress strongly support a dissociative etiology (F44.8, Other dissociative [conversion] disorders) rather than focal impaired awareness seizures.
